plan_a_advantages: Includes tempo runs to improve sustainable effort and race-specific rhythm.
Incorporates interval training to enhance speed and efficiency.
Features a strength training session focused on leg muscles and incline work, supporting injury resistance and power.
Higher overall training volume (315 minutes vs 300) allows for more adaptation.
plan_b_advantages: Emphasizes aerobic endurance with a greater focus on easy-paced runs.
Lower overall training volume may be suitable for athletes with a higher risk of injury or those new to structured training.
Includes a strength and mobility session, though less frequent than Plan A.
reasoning: While both plans incorporate essential elements for trail running improvement, Plan A is the better choice for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. Plan A includes tempo and interval sessions, which are crucial for developing speed and race-specific rhythm – elements absent in Plan B. The inclusion of higher intensity workouts allows for greater physiological adaptation and ultimately, faster running. Plan B focuses almost exclusively on aerobic endurance at easy paces, which is important but insufficient for achieving a significant speed increase.
